title: He looks strong. Connected. Blessed.
paragraphs:
He looks strong. Connected. Blessed.
But not everyone you see flourishing is rooted in God.

Jeremiah 17:7 (NIV):
“But blessed is the one who trusts in the Lord, whose confidence is in Him.”
Pause there.

Not blessed because of hustle.
Not blessed because of connections.
Not blessed because life is easy.
Blessed because of trust.

And that word—trust—is not soft.
It’s war.

It means when money is low… you still obey.
When doors close… you still believe.
When prayers feel unanswered… you still stay.

That’s not weakness.
That’s covenant loyalty.
But here’s what we miss…

We want the blessing of verse 7,
without surrendering like the man in verse 8.

The one who becomes like a tree—
roots deep, leaves green,
unshaken by heat, unafraid of drought.
Why?

Because his source is not the season.
His source is God.

Listen—
You can have a good life without God for a moment…
but you cannot have a rooted life without Him forever.

So the real question is not:
“Am I blessed?”

It’s this:
“Where is my trust anchored?”

Because whatever you trust in—
that’s what you draw life from.

And if it’s not Jesus…
it will fail you.

But if it is Christ—
crucified for your sin,
risen for your salvation—

then even in drought,
you will not wither.

You will stand.
You will bear fruit.
You will live.

Not because you’re strong.
But because He is faithful.
